notes: The printed format repeats {implementor-name-1 | literal-1} (refuter rendered page 438), so a list is format-legal. But GR4 gives a meaning only to 'a storage medium referenced by implementor-name-1 or literal-1'. The standard never says what a second operand references, and SR3 hands both the meaning and the allowable content of each implementor-name-1 and literal-1 to the implementor. One allowable rule is 'one operand names the file, optionally after a device class'. ISO 2023 prints the same list and words the latitude as 'the allowable specification' (SR5), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-71 records the determination under rule 1 precedence (GnuCOBOL). The refusal is by name (COBOL2256, citing the entry), never a generic syntax error. The single-operand association works (the adjudicator's probes; p10's refusal names DOC-A.1-71). ATTACK SURFACE: the refuter's reading, that 1985 'content' covers what each operand holds and not how many operands there are. If that reading wins, the row is PARTIAL with harm rejects_legal_source, and the fix gives a list an implementor-defined meaning.
